# Navigation — Agent Plan (UKCheckpoints, Flutter + HERE Navigate SDK)

Build a turn-by-turn experience that holds up to real drivers doing dumb things: swiping the map mid-drive, losing GPS in a tunnel, rage-tapping buttons, tapping the map while typing an address, reopening a sheet and expecting it exactly how they left it.

This file is the source of truth. `todo.md` is the executable task list. Read both before writing code.

---

## Paths (where everything lives)

**Plan docs (write/update these):**
- `plan/navigation.md` — this file. Source of truth.
- `plan/todo.md` — executable task list.

**Local HERE SDK docs (read these BEFORE coding — do not guess APIs):**
- `here-sdk_doc_local/` — the offline HERE SDK documentation on the machine. **This is the primary reference. Read it before every nav API decision.**
- Maneuver icon assets: `here-sdk_doc_local/heresdk-flutter-4.25.5.0-dev-guide/graphics/maneuver_icons/` — copy the required icons from here into the project assets.
- Confirm the SDK version: the doc folder name (`...-4.25.5.0-...`) and `pubspec.yaml` must agree. If they don't, the doc wins for behavior — re-pin or re-verify. Camera-behavior APIs (§3) exist on 4.25.x, so that path is correct for this version.

**Project feature root:** `lib/features/navigation/` — the module tree in §10 is rooted here. Every path in §10 is relative to this root (e.g. `lib/features/navigation/utils/strings.dart`).

---

## 0. Hard rules (read once, obey always)

- **Read `here-sdk_doc_local/` first.** Before writing any navigation code, read the relevant pages in the local doc folder. Do not rely on memory or assume a method exists.

- **Verify every API against HERE docs before using it.** Do not assume a method exists. The relevant verified primitives are listed in §3. If you need one not listed there, confirm it in the SDK API reference for the *exact* SDK version pinned in `pubspec.yaml` first.
- **UK units only.** Miles for long distance, yards for close maneuvers. Never km, never metres, never feet. Hardcode the formatter so a European device locale cannot override it. See §2.
- **Plain English UI.** No "Destination", "Guidance", "Maneuver", "Origin". See the dictionary in §1.
- **No `setState` storms.** Sheet and navigation state live in dedicated state objects (Riverpod / Zustand-equiv). Reopening a sheet rebuilds from retained state, never re-fetches, never resets scroll/inputs. See §6.
- **Single responsibility per file.** No giant widgets, no business logic in UI. Module layout in §9.
- **Production-ready only.** No placeholder UI, no debug styling, no oversized buttons, no wasted spacing, no nested-scroll traps. Works on small phone, large phone, tablet.

---

## 1. Plain English UI dictionary

A tired driver should never have to translate the interface. Swap every technical term at the UI layer (keep SDK names internal in code).

| Internal / SDK term        | UI string                          |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| Destination                | **Going to**                       |
| Origin / current location  | **Start** / **My location**        |
| Start guidance / navigate  | **Start drive** / **Let's go**     |
| Maneuver                   | **Next turn**                      |
| Recalculating              | **Finding a new route…**           |
| Route preview              | **Trip overview**                  |
| Terminate guidance         | **End trip** / **Stop**            |
| Reroute / deviation        | (silent to user; just re-route)    |
| Destination reached        | **You've arrived**                 |

Centralise these in one `strings.dart` (or i18n file). No inline literals scattered across widgets.

---

## 2. UK localization (units)

- **Routing request:** force Imperial UK. Set the route options / measurement system to UK imperial when calling the routing engine. Do not rely on the device.
- **Visual navigator + voice:** configure unit system explicitly to UK so spoken and on-screen text read "In 300 yards, turn left" and "2.4 miles".
- **Distance formatter (the safety net):** write one pure function. It is the only place distance → string happens.
  - `< 0.1 mi` → round to nearest 10 yards, show `"{n} yards"`.
  - `>= 0.1 mi` → show miles to 1 decimal under 10 mi, whole/half miles above.
  - Never emit "km", "m", "ft" — not even as a fallback. If input is ambiguous, assume metres-in, convert out; never pass through device locale.
- **Speed:** mph only.

---

## 3. Verified HERE SDK primitives (the load-bearing ones)

These are confirmed against the HERE SDK for Flutter (Navigate Edition) docs. Treat as the allowed surface; confirm signatures against your pinned version.

**Navigator / rendering**
- `VisualNavigator` — same method signatures as `Navigator`, plus rendering. Use it.
- `visualNavigator.startRendering(mapView)` — adds the interpolated 3D arrow marker; location updates are smoothly interpolated by the SDK. **Do not build custom interpolation — the SDK already does it.**
- `visualNavigator.stopRendering()` — tear down rendering.
- `visualNavigator.route = route` — sets route, leaves tracking mode. Setting it with no route → tracking mode.
- `VisualNavigator` conforms to `LocationListener` (`onLocationUpdated`). Feed it locations from a location provider; SDK does map-matching.

**Camera (the core of the "camera fucks off then comes back" loop)**
- `visualNavigator.cameraBehavior` — the follow engine. Settable at any time during navigation.
  - `DynamicCameraBehavior()` → auto-zooms in/out around maneuvers. Default choice for active drive.
  - `FixedCameraBehavior()` → fixed distance/tilt/bearing. Configurable via `setCameraDistanceInMeters`, `setCameraTiltInDegrees`, `setCameraBearingInDegrees(null)` for north-up off.
  - **`cameraBehavior = null` → camera released. The arrow keeps moving, the map does not.** This is the "free" state after the user pans.
- (Deprecated, do **not** use: `CameraMode`, `CameraSettings`, `cameraMode`, `cameraSettings`.)

**Gestures (detecting the user grabbing the map)**
- `mapView.gestures` exposes per-gesture listeners (pan, pinch, two-finger pan, long-press, tap, etc.).
- Continuous gestures report a `begin` state — use that, not `update`.
- Setting a listener does **not** disable the default map action. Keep pan working; just listen.
- `gestures.disableDefaultAction(GestureType.x)` exists but is **not** what we want here — we want the user to be able to pan.

**Guidance events (subscribe to these, never read off the Route object during a drive)**
- `eventTextListener` / maneuver notification text → for voice TTS + the turn banner.
- Route progress listener → traveled distance, remaining distance/duration, current + next maneuver, section progress. **This is the source for the progress bar and ETA. Never use time-based estimates.**
- Route deviation listener → fires when user leaves the route. Trigger reroute.
- Destination reached listener → fires on arrival. Trigger the arrival flow.
- Speed / safety-camera warners → optional, for speed indicator.

**Routing / search**
- Routing engine → `Route` with geometry, maneuvers, ETA, distance, duration.
- Search engine → autosuggest / autocomplete, geocoding, reverse geocoding. Used by the search sheet.

If a capability you need isn't above, **stop and read `here-sdk_doc_local/` (and its API reference) before coding.** Do not invent a method name.

---

## 4. The bottom sheet system

Three primary states. State is retained — see §6 for the no-rerender / restore rule.

**Peek (default, ~80–120px)** — "Where to?" field, map is primary, all checkpoint markers visible, no route.

**Full search** — triggered by tapping the search field. Shows:
- **Start** input — defaults to current location (icon + address), editable / removable / searchable.
- **Going to** input — empty, autosuggest-driven.
- **Swap** button between them — swaps Start/Going-to with an animated transition.
- Search: HERE autosuggest, **250ms debounce**, with loading / empty / error states. Suggestions show place name, full address, category icon. Tapping a suggestion autofills and drops the keyboard.
- When both points are valid → primary CTA **Let's go** appears (only when a route can actually be computed).

**Trip overview (half sheet)** — after route is computed (see §7).

---

## 5. Checkpoints along the route (filtering + smooth async)

**Normal mode:** all global checkpoint markers shown.

**Route mode:** hide global checkpoints; show only checkpoints within **300m of the route geometry** ("route checkpoints").

**This calculation is async and can be slow — that's fine.** Compute the route-checkpoint set off the UI thread (isolate / background). While it runs, **show a loading state in the checkpoint section** of the sheet, not a frozen UI and not a blank list. When done, render in. Do not block route preview on it — the route, ETA and map can show immediately; checkpoints stream in when ready.

Each route checkpoint carries: name, status (`active` / `alert` / `closed` / `unknown`), last-updated time, distance along route. Sort by distance along route. Render status visually.

**Tap a checkpoint:** move sheet to Peek, focus + smooth-zoom map on it, open its details.

**Exit route mode:** restore global checkpoints + original map state, drop the route-checkpoint filter.

---

## 6. State retention — no re-render, no reset (your explicit requirement)

The failure you called out: you're mid-task in the sheet, you peek it down, you reopen it, and it's wiped or it re-renders everything. Fix:

- Sheet content state (active inputs, typed text, cursor, scroll offset, computed suggestions, the current route, the route-checkpoint list) lives in a **persistent state object outside the widget tree**. Peeking/expanding only changes a `sheetHeight` / `sheetMode` value — it does **not** dispose or rebuild the content.
- Reopening restores the exact prior state. No re-fetch, no re-debounce, no scroll jump.
- Widget identity preserved (stable keys, no conditional remount of the whole subtree). Only the things that actually changed rebuild.
- **The "changed my mind" input:** tapping the map while Full Search is open instantly drops the keyboard, unfocuses the field, and peeks the sheet — **without** discarding what was typed. Reopening shows it again.

---

## 7. Trip overview (route preview)

Computing a route moves the sheet Full → Half and shows:

- **Trip summary card:** ETA, arrival time, distance remaining, travel duration, going-to name + full address.
- **Route checkpoint section:** route checkpoints + warnings/alerts/active events, sorted by distance along route (loads async per §5).
- **Next turn preview:** first maneuver icon + instruction + distance to it.
- **Primary action: Start drive.** Secondary: **Close** (returns to planning; restores global checkpoints + map).

Map: focus on the route, show start + going-to markers + route polyline, fit camera to the whole route.

---

## 8. Active drive (turn-by-turn) — the camera control loop

This is the part you care most about. Read carefully.

When **Start drive** is pressed:
- `visualNavigator.startRendering(mapView)`, set `visualNavigator.route`, set `visualNavigator.cameraBehavior = DynamicCameraBehavior()`. Sheet auto-collapses to Peek. Search UI is replaced by the navigation header.
- A `NavigationPhase` sealed state drives everything. Camera ownership is an explicit sub-state: `CameraFollowing` vs `CameraFree`.

**The "let go of the camera" loop (exact mechanic):**

1. **Following (default):** `cameraBehavior` is set (Dynamic). HERE owns the camera — it auto-pans, tilts ~45°, auto-zooms around turns, follows the arrow. We do not touch the camera in this state.
2. **User grabs the map:** `PanListener` on `mapView.gestures` fires on **`GestureState.begin`** (not `update` — `update` fires every frame and will thrash). On begin:
   - set `visualNavigator.cameraBehavior = null` → **the SDK releases the camera. Arrow keeps moving, map stays where the user dragged it.** This is the "camera, fuck off for now" state.
   - transition to `CameraFree`.
   - show a large, high-contrast **Recenter** button (bottom-right, thumb-reachable). The arrow / location indicator keeps updating; routing, progress, ETA, reroute, checkpoints all keep updating **in the background regardless of camera state** — camera ownership is purely visual and never gates data.
3. **Coming back:** two ways back to Following, both restore HERE's camera behavior:
   - user taps **Recenter**, or
   - debounced idle timer (no map interaction for ~10s) auto-recenters.
   - On either: `visualNavigator.cameraBehavior = DynamicCameraBehavior()` again → SDK smoothly takes the camera back ("filmy" return is the SDK's interpolated re-acquisition; don't hand-animate it). Hide the Recenter button. Transition to `CameraFollowing`.

Do **not** disable pan gestures during the drive — the user is allowed to look around. We only toggle *who owns the camera*, via `cameraBehavior`.

**Navigation header (replaces search bar entirely):**
- **Primary next turn (always visible):** maneuver icon + plain instruction + distance ("Turn right" / "In 500 yards"). Large type, high contrast.
- **Secondary turn:** shown only when next maneuver ≤ ~500 yards away ("Then keep left, after 200 yards"). Otherwise hidden completely.

**Navigation card (bottom):** ETA, remaining distance, remaining duration. Controls: **End trip**; optional **Mute** and **Recenter**.

**Progress bar:** `traveledDistance / totalRouteDistance` from the route-progress event (never time-based). Render checkpoint indicators along the bar at their position-along-route, colored by status (`active` / `alert` / `closed`; **never show `unknown`** on the bar). Animate a checkpoint to "completed" as the user passes it.

**All real-time updates come from HERE navigation events** — position, progress, ETA, remaining distance/duration, current + upcoming maneuver, checkpoint states. Position smoothing is the SDK's interpolation via `startRendering` — do not reinvent it.

---

## 9. Edge cases — "users do dumb things"

| State | Trigger | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Detached camera** (§8) | User pans during drive | `cameraBehavior = null`, show Recenter, auto-recenter after ~10s idle. |
| **Tunnel / GPS loss** | HERE GPS signal/accuracy drops below usable threshold | **Do not cancel the route.** Grey out the speed indicator, show a **"Searching for GPS…"** banner, hold last known position, lean on SDK interpolation. Recover silently when signal returns. |
| **Rage tap** | Double/triple-tap on Let's go / Swap / any network button | Strict state lock. While `isRouting == true` the button is visually disabled and ignores taps. Show a spinner on the **first** tap immediately. Applies to every network-calling button. |
| **Changed my mind** | Taps map while typing an address (Full Search open) | Drop keyboard, unfocus, peek sheet — **without** discarding typed text (§6). |
| **Reroute** | RouteDeviation event | Silently reroute. Recompute ETA, route checkpoints, maneuver list. Show **"Finding a new route…"** briefly. Update UI seamlessly — no flash, no reset of camera state. |
| **Arrived** | DestinationReached event | Stop navigation + rendering. Remove route polyline, route checkpoints, nav UI. Restore global checkpoints + standard search. Show a clear **"You've arrived"** state (name + address), then settle back to Peek. |

---

## 10. Module layout

Rooted at `lib/features/navigation/`. Every subfolder below is relative to that root.

```
lib/features/navigation/
├── widgets/        # dumb presentational widgets
├── sheets/         # peek / full-search / trip-overview sheets (state-retaining)
├── routing/        # route calc, options (UK imperial forced here)
├── checkpoints/    # route-checkpoint filtering (async/isolate), markers, progress indicators
├── maneuvers/      # maneuver icon mapping, primary/secondary turn widgets
├── navigation/     # VisualNavigator lifecycle, camera-ownership state machine, event listeners
├── search/         # autosuggest, debounce, suggestion list
├── models/         # NavigationPhase sealed state, CheckpointStatus, etc.
├── providers/      # state objects (sheet state, nav state) — survive sheet collapse
├── services/       # location provider, GPS-quality, TTS
└── utils/          # UK distance/speed formatter (single source), strings.dart
```

Single responsibility per file. No business logic in UI. No file large enough to scroll forever.

---

## 11. Maneuver icons

Copy the maneuver icon set from `here-sdk_doc_local/heresdk-flutter-4.25.5.0-dev-guide/graphics/maneuver_icons/` into the project assets (e.g. `assets/maneuver_icons/`, registered in `pubspec.yaml`). Map each SDK maneuver action → one asset in `lib/features/navigation/maneuvers/`. Verify the action enum against the local doc; don't assume icon filenames — check what's actually in the `maneuver_icons` folder.

---

## 12. Definition of done (per feature, before marking a `todo.md` box)

- Verified against HERE docs for the pinned SDK version.
- UK units only; passed the formatter, no km/m/ft anywhere in output.
- Plain-English strings, no SDK jargon surfaced.
- Survives: pan-during-drive, GPS loss, rage tap, map-tap-while-typing, reroute, arrival.
- Sheet collapse → reopen restores exact state, no re-fetch, no rerender storm.
- Works on small phone, large phone, tablet.
- Build + analyze clean.

---

## 13. Custom vehicles (SQLite-backed, feeds route + turn-by-turn)

The user can pick a vehicle type *and* save their own custom vehicles. The chosen vehicle is not cosmetic — its parameters go into route calculation **and** into active turn-by-turn, so speed limits, road restrictions, and ETA reflect that actual vehicle. HERE supports this directly; do not fake it.

### Verified HERE surface (read `here-sdk_doc_local/` to confirm signatures for 4.25.5.0)

- **Per-mode route options** passed to the routing engine's `calculateRoute()` overloads:
  - `CarOptions`, `TruckOptions`, `ScooterOptions`, `PedestrianOptions`, `TaxiOptions`, `EVCarOptions`, `EVTruckOptions`.
- **Custom specs live inside the options:**
  - `TruckOptions` holds `TruckSpecifications` (dimensions: height, width, length; `grossWeightInKilograms`, `weightPerAxleInKilograms`, axle count, etc.) and an optional `SpeedProfile`.
  - Common `RouteOptions` (alternatives count, `OptimizationMode`) sits inside every mode's options.
  - `AvoidanceOptions` (e.g. exclude emission zones, toll roads, tunnels) — expose as toggles per saved vehicle.
- **Turn-by-turn must also know the vehicle:** the navigator has its own profile.
  - `navigator.trackingTransportProfile(vehicleProfile)` with a `VehicleProfile` (transport mode + `VehicleSpecification`). **Default is car if unset.** For a truck/custom vehicle you must set this or the live speed-limit (CVR) warnings and notifications will be wrong.
  - When a route is set, the navigator uses the route's profile; for tracking mode (no route) set the transport profile explicitly.
- **Weight/dimensions are not labels.** `grossWeightInKilograms` and dimensions change CVR speed limits, route restrictions, and ETA. A wrong spec produces a wrong route silently — validate inputs.

> ⚠️ Units note: HERE vehicle specs are SI (kilograms, metres/centimetres). The UK rule in §2 applies to **display only**. Store and pass SI internally; convert at the UI edge (the user may type tonnes / feet-inches — convert in the form, persist SI).

### Data model + SQLite (clean repository pattern)

One table, one repository, no SDK types leaking into storage.

```sql
-- migration: vehicles
CREATE TABLE vehicles (
  id              TEXT PRIMARY KEY,         -- uuid
  name            TEXT NOT NULL,            -- "My Van", "Work Lorry"
  transport_mode  TEXT NOT NULL,            -- car | truck | scooter | pedestrian | taxi | ev_car | ev_truck
  is_default      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  -- specs (SI units, nullable for car/scooter)
  gross_weight_kg INTEGER,
  height_cm       INTEGER,
  width_cm        INTEGER,
  length_cm       INTEGER,
  axle_count      INTEGER,
  -- avoidance toggles (0/1)
  avoid_tolls     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  avoid_tunnels   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,

```

Layers (each its own file, single responsibility — §10):
- `models/vehicle.dart` — plain Dart `Vehicle` model. No HERE imports.
- `services/vehicle_repository.dart` — `VehicleRepository` interface: `watchAll()`, `getById()`, `getDefault()`, `upsert(Vehicle)`, `delete(id)`, `setDefault(id)`. SQLite implementation behind it. **No SDK types in this layer.**
- `routing/vehicle_mapper.dart` — the ONLY place that converts a `Vehicle` → HERE route options (`CarOptions`/`TruckOptions`/…) **and** → `VehicleProfile` for the navigator. Pure functions, unit-tested. Keeps SDK coupling in one file.
- `providers/vehicle_provider.dart` — selected vehicle + list, retained like other nav state (§6).

### Default vehicles + custom

- On first run, seed a small set of sensible **defaults** (e.g. "Car", "Walk") matching HERE's built-in modes so the list is never empty. `is_default = 1`, not user-deletable (or restorable).
- "Add vehicle" form: pick transport mode → reveal only the fields that mode supports (truck shows weight/dimensions; car shows almost nothing; pedestrian shows none). Validate ranges. Persist as SI. The form is where UK→SI conversion happens.
- The user's chosen vehicle persists as the selected one (`getDefault()` / explicit selection) across app restarts.

### Where it plugs into the existing flow

- **Trip overview (§7):** show a vehicle selector (chips/row) listing all saved vehicles + defaults. Each row can show that vehicle's computed ETA/time for this trip. Tapping a vehicle **recalculates the route** with that vehicle's mapped options (`vehicle_mapper.dart`), under the same rage-tap interaction lock (§9) and a loading state — recompute is async, so show a spinner on the selected chip, not a frozen sheet.
- **Start drive (§8):** set both the route (already vehicle-specific) and `navigator.trackingTransportProfile(...)` from the same `Vehicle` via the mapper, so live warnings match.
- **Reroute (§9):** reuse the currently selected vehicle's options — never silently fall back to car.

---

## 14. User stories (so the flow *feels* right)

These are narrative, not spec. Read them to understand intended texture — typing, debounce, loading states, when buttons appear, what the camera does. The numbered sections above are authoritative on behavior; these stories show how it should feel in sequence.

### Story A — The success path ("it just worked")

Sara opens the app. The map fills the screen with her local checkpoints dotted around; a slim sheet sits at the bottom: **"Where to?"** She taps it. The sheet glides to full height. **Start** is already filled — "My location" with hacer current street under it. The cursor lands in **Going to**. She types "brist". After a beat (the 250ms debounce — not on every keystroke) a short list appears: "Bristol Temple Meads", full address, a station icon. She taps it. Keyboard drops, field fills. A **Let's go** button fades in at the bottom — it wasn't there a second ago because there was nothing to route yet.

She taps **Let's go** once. The button shows a spinner immediately and ignores her thumb when she taps again out of habit. The sheet settles to half height: **Trip overview** — 2.4 miles, arrive 14:38, 9 min, "Bristol Temple Meads". A vehicle row shows "Car" selected. Below, a checkpoint section is briefly showing a loading shimmer, then three route checkpoints slide in, sorted by how soon she'll reach them. The first turn preview reads "Turn right onto Victoria St, in 200 yards." She taps **Start drive**.

The sheet drops to a peek. The map tilts into the 3D follow view, her arrow gliding smoothly even between GPS pings. A big banner up top: **"Turn right — in 200 yards."** She drives. The progress bar fills left to right; a checkpoint dot she passes animates to "done." At her destination the guidance stops, the route and its checkpoints clear, her global checkpoints return, and a calm **"You've arrived"** card shows the name and address before settling back to the peek sheet.

### Story B — The dumb-user path ("fat fingers and impatience")

Dave is driving with the app already guiding him. A notification buzzes; he swipes the screen to dismiss it and accidentally drags the map sideways. The car arrow keeps moving but the map now shows empty fields a mile away — the camera **let go** the instant his finger moved it (`cameraBehavior = null`). A large **Recenter** button appears bottom-right. Dave ignores it for a few seconds while at a light; after about 10 seconds of no touching, the map smoothly slides back behind his arrow on its own and the button disappears. The route, his ETA, the next turn — none of it ever paused; only the camera had wandered.

Earlier, before setting off, Dave had triple-tapped **Let's go** because he's impatient. It spun on the first tap and swallowed the other two — no double route, no flicker. And while typing his destination he'd second-guessed himself and tapped the map; the keyboard dropped, the sheet peeked down, but when he tapped the search field again his half-typed "manche…" was still sitting there. Nothing he did broke it.

### Story C — The error / bad-conditions path ("the tunnel and the wrong turn")

Priya is driving a route when she enters a long tunnel. GPS degrades. The speed readout greys out and a quiet banner appears: **"Searching for GPS…"** The app does **not** cancel her trip or fling her marker into a river — it holds her last known position and leans on the SDK's interpolation. She exits the tunnel; the banner vanishes and tracking resumes cleanly without her doing anything.

A minute later she misses a turn. The app detects the deviation, shows **"Finding a new route…"** for a moment, and quietly recalculates — new ETA, refreshed route checkpoints, updated turns — using her selected vehicle's options, not a reset-to-car. The camera stays in whatever state it was in; no jarring jump. She never had to tap anything.

### Story D — The struggle-then-success path ("custom vehicle, learning the app")

Tom drives a 3.5-tonne box van and the default "Car" route keeps sending him down a low-bridge road. First time, he's confused — the route looks wrong for his van. He finds **Add vehicle** in the vehicle row on the trip overview. He picks **Truck**, and only then do weight and height fields appear. He types his weight in tonnes and height in feet-and-inches (the form converts to SI for him), names it **"Work Van"**, saves. It's now in his list, persisted — it'll be there next time he opens the app.

Back on the trip overview he taps **Work Van**. The chip spins briefly while the route recalculates with his van's weight and dimensions; the new route avoids the low bridge and the ETA updates. He taps **Start drive** — and now the live speed-limit warnings reflect commercial-vehicle limits, because the navigator got his `VehicleProfile` too, not just the route. What started as a wrong, frustrating route became a correct one once the app knew what he was actually driving.===# TODO — Navigation (UKCheckpoints)

1	# AGENTS.md
2	
3	## Role
4	
5	You are an autonomous senior Flutter cleanup engineer.
6	
7	Inspect one requested folder or feature area, clean it up, verify it, open one focused PR. That's the whole job.
8	
9	You are not redesigning the app, inventing architecture, adding features, or writing clever code. You are making the existing Flutter iOS/Android codebase cleaner, safer, faster, and easier for the next engineer (and real users) to understand.
10	
11	## First Rule
12	
13	Before anything, ask the user which folder or feature to work on. Do not inspect, edit, or plan until you have the target path.
14	
15	That path is the only editable scope. Everything else is read-only context.
16

18	- You may read outside it to learn project conventions.
19	- You may not edit outside it without explicit approval.
20

22	
23	## HERE SDK — local docs (I HAVE Navigation Tier so i have Licesense for it.)
24	
25	You do not have HERE SDK / `here-sdk` knowledge in your head. Do not guess HERE API names, signatures, routing params, map options, or asset paths from memory.
26	
27	A full local copy of the HERE SDK API reference, docs, and examples is set up in `here-sdk_local_doc/`. Use it as the source of truth. Find what you need with plain shell:
28	
29	```sh
30	# locate the doc tree (don't assume the exact location)
31	find . -type d -name "here-sdk_local_doc"
32	
33	# find an API, class, or method
34	grep -rn "HERE.routing.RoutingEngine" here-sdk_local_doc/
35	grep -rni "bottom sheet" here-sdk_local_doc/
36	
37	# find an example or asset to reuse
38	grep -rln "MapMarker" here-sdk_local_doc/
39	find here-sdk_local_doc/ -name "*.png" -o -name "*.svg"
40	```
41	
42	Read the local doc or example before calling any HERE API. If it isn't in `here-sdk_local_doc/`, say so — don't invent it.
43	
44	## HERE SDK — use the SDK, never reinvent it
45	
46	**If HERE SDK provides it, use it. Never build a custom version.**
47	
48	Before writing any navigation, routing, mapping, or location code, check whether the SDK already does it. The SDK covers:
49	
50	- **Location smoothing / interpolation** — `VisualNavigator.startRendering()` handles it. Do not write custom interpolation between GPS pings.
51	- **Camera follow** — `DynamicCameraBehavior()` / `FixedCameraBehavior()`. Do not hand-animate the camera.
52	- **Autosuggest / geocoding** — `SearchEngine`. Do not call a third-party geocoder or write a custom debounce layer around a raw HTTP search API.
53	- **Route calculation** — `RoutingEngine.calculateRouteWithRoutingOptions()`. Do not build a custom routing client.
54	- **Map matching** — `Navigator` / `VisualNavigator` feeds on `LocationListener`; the SDK map-matches internally. Do not write your own snap-to-road logic.
55	- **Maneuver icons** — already in `here-sdk_doc_local/.../graphics/maneuver_icons/`. Do not generate, draw, or source icons from elsewhere.
56	- **Turn-by-turn instructions** — `ManeuverNotificationListener` / route-progress listener provides text and distance. Do not compute instructions from raw geometry.
57	- **Speed-limit warnings** — `SpeedWarningListener`. Do not derive speed limits from raw map data.
58	- **Progress / ETA** — `RouteProgressListener`. Never compute progress or ETA from elapsed time.
59	
60	The rule: **grep the local package source (`packages/here_sdk/lib/`) and docs (`here-sdk_doc_local/`) first. If the capability exists there, use it. Only write custom code for things the SDK genuinely does not provide.**
61	
62	## Engineering Standard
63	
64	Write boring code only. Boring means: clear names, small files, small widgets, simple control flow, predictable state, obvious folder structure. No magic abstractions, no clever one-liners, no unnecessary packages, no framework cosplay, no sci-fi architecture names.
65

2. **Load the industry pack.** Read the matching file from `references/`:
   - `industry-saas.md` for SaaS / app interfaces
   - `industry-corporate.md` for marketing sites
   - `industry-engineering.md` for B2B, data-dense, industrial
   - `industry-mobile-ios.md` for iOS native + Flutter Cupertino
   - `industry-mobile-android.md` for Android native + Flutter Material
3. **Run the 25 anti-slop rules** in `references/anti-slop-rules.md`. These are checked
   on output, not just on intent.
4. **Pull tokens from foundation.** `references/foundation.md` has the OKLCH palette,
   spacing scale, radius scale, motion curves, and the Tailwind v4 `@theme` block.
5. **Cross-check components.** `references/components.md` has spec for every primitive
   with hard limits and escape hatches.
6. **Self-review before shipping.** Walk the output against the anti-slop checklist
   and report any rule violations with the override reason.

If you skip step 1, the output regresses to median AI slop. The calibration is the
single biggest lever in the entire system.

---

## REFERENCE FILES

Read these on demand, not all at once. Each is the authoritative source for its domain.

| File | When to load |
|---|---|
| `references/anti-slop-rules.md` | **Always** load before generating any UI |
| `references/foundation.md` | **Always** load — color, type, spacing, radius, motion tokens |
| `references/components.md` | Whenever generating buttons, forms, cards, tables, modals, lists, badges |
| `references/typography.md` | Picking typefaces, optical sizing, font pairings |
| `references/motion.md` | Any animation, transition, or interactive feedback |
| `references/accessibility.md` | WCAG 2.2 AA — every component must pass |
| `references/seo-clean-code.md` | Marketing sites, semantic HTML, Core Web Vitals |
| `references/tailwind-v4.md` | Setting up `@theme`, OKLCH tokens, container queries |
| `references/shadcn.md` | Customizing shadcn/ui without producing default-neutral slop |
| `references/industry-saas.md` | SaaS pack — Linear/Vercel/Stripe/Raycast grammar |
| `references/industry-corporate.md` | Corporate / marketing pack — Apple/Stripe/Anthropic |
| `references/industry-engineering.md` | B2B / data-dense / industrial pack |
| `references/industry-mobile-ios.md` | iOS 26 Liquid Glass mobile pack |
| `references/industry-mobile-android.md` | Material 3 Expressive mobile pack |

---

## THE FIVE LAWS

These override everything. If a request conflicts with a Law, push back before complying.

### Law 1 — Calibrate the personality before writing code.
SaaS app and marketing site live by different rules. Engineering tool and consumer
mobile app live by different rules. Without a personality decision, every interface
regresses to the same `bg-indigo-500` + Inter + `rounded-2xl` median. Make the
personality decision explicit at the top of every component or screen file (a comment
is fine).

### Law 2 — One accent color, semantic everything else.
The brand has exactly one accent. Status colors (success / warning / error / info) are
semantic, never branded. Neutral fills 90% of the surface. Three-or-more-color brand
palettes are banned in the default pack — only marketing hero gradients (Stripe-style
mesh) allow multi-hue, and only inside a clearly bounded section.

### Law 3 — Hierarchy comes from color and weight before size.
Body text is one size. Display heads are one size larger. Secondary text is the same
size as body but with reduced opacity or a muted token. Stop scaling text up and down
to communicate importance. Pull the reader's eye with weight (400 → 500 → 600) and
contrast (foreground → muted → subtle), not with 12px ↔ 18px noise.

### Law 4 — Motion only when it changes meaning.
Animate state changes, modal entries, list reorders, optimistic confirmations. Do not
animate keyboard-initiated actions, frequently-used dropdowns, or anything triggered
more than 50× per session. Frequency kills delight; reach for instant. Emil Kowalski's
rule: Raycast has no open animation because the user opens it hundreds of times a day.

### Law 5 — Density is a feature, not a bug.
2026's reference brands all moved toward higher density (Linear's calmer interface,
Stripe Sigma's tables, Datadog dashboards). Whitespace is a tool, not a default. For
app interfaces, prefer table rows 40–48px tall, list items at native platform minimums,
and information per screen over "breathing room." Marketing sites are the only place
generous whitespace is the default.

---

## THE 25 ANTI-SLOP RULES (SUMMARY)

The full rules with rationale and primary sources live in `references/anti-slop-rules.md`.
This is the shortlist for quick reference:

1. No `bg-indigo-500`, no `from-indigo-500 to-purple-600` gradients, no Tailwind default purple.
2. No center-stacked "H1 + subtitle + 2 CTAs" hero.
3. Inter is fine, but Inter + default Tailwind + default shadcn = instant slop. Differentiate.
4. No `rounded-2xl` or `rounded-3xl` on every surface. Pick a radius system per industry pack.
5. No three-column "icon + heading + paragraph" features grid as a default layout.
6. Card-everything syndrome is banned. Tables, lists, prose blocks exist.
7. The stock dashboard layout (sidebar + topbar + 4 stat cards + table) needs differentiation.
8. No ✨ sparkle emoji. No AI iconography. Don't telegraph the tool.
9. No glassmorphism on every surface. Glass is contextual (iOS Liquid Glass, specific overlays).
10. No 3D abstract humans, no floating geometric shapes, no unDraw / Storyset.
11. No generic CTA pair ("Get started for free" + "Watch demo"). Single CTA per section.
12. No "Trusted by" grayscale logo wall as a default.
13. The shadcn default neutral theme is banned. Override `--primary`, `--radius`, font.
14. No lorem-ipsum-feeling copy. Concrete copy referencing the real user and outcome.
15. No drop shadows on everything. Use background contrast for elevation.
16. No pure `#000` text on `#fff`. Use desaturated near-black (`oklch(20% 0.04 265)`).
17. No default Material/Bootstrap blue links. Match brand or use a neutral underline.
18. No full-viewport hero gradient backgrounds as default.
19. No identical card hover (`scale(1.05) + shadow-2xl`). Translate-Y + border shift.
20. No loading spinner that causes layout shift. Fixed-width buttons swap label for spinner.
21. No modal-centered-with-blur on mobile. Use bottom sheet (Vaul).
22. No flat-illustration empty states with "No data yet" headline. Explain what the screen becomes.
23. No auto-animate on enter for everything. Animate only what changes meaning.
24. Body text below 15px is banned. 16px desktop minimum, 17px mobile.
25. No body fonts at weight 300 — illegible at small sizes.

---

## TAILWIND V4 @theme — DEFAULT TOKENS

Drop this into the project's CSS. Tokens are OKLCH for perceptually-uniform scales.
Industry packs override `--color-accent`, `--radius-button`, `--font-display`, and a
small set of duration tokens. Everything else stays.

```css
@import "tailwindcss";

@theme {
  /* === Color: semantic, OKLCH, one accent === */
  --color-bg: oklch(99% 0.004 270);
  --color-fg: oklch(20% 0.04 265);
  --color-muted: oklch(55% 0.02 270);
  --color-subtle: oklch(75% 0.015 270);
  --color-border: oklch(92% 0.005 270);
  --color-surface: oklch(98% 0.003 270);
  --color-surface-2: oklch(96% 0.004 270);

  --color-accent: oklch(60% 0.18 250);          /* override per pack */
  --color-accent-fg: oklch(99% 0.005 250);
  --color-accent-soft: oklch(96% 0.04 250);

  --color-success: oklch(65% 0.16 145);
  --color-warning: oklch(75% 0.14 75);
  --color-error: oklch(60% 0.22 25);
  --color-info: oklch(65% 0.13 230);

  /* === Dark mode === */
  /* override via .dark { --color-bg: oklch(15% 0.02 270); ... } */

  /* === Radius: system, not random === */
  --radius-input: 0.375rem;        /* 6px - inputs, small cards */
  --radius-card: 0.5rem;           /* 8px - cards, surfaces */
  --radius-button: 9999px;         /* capsule by default */
  --radius-modal: 0.75rem;         /* 12px - dialogs */

  /* === Spacing: 4px base === */
  /* Tailwind v4 provides this automatically; just use the scale */

  /* === Typography === */
  --font-sans: "Geist", "Inter", system-ui, sans-serif;
  --font-mono: "Geist Mono", "JetBrains Mono", ui-monospace, monospace;
  --font-display: "Geist", "Inter Display", "Inter", system-ui, sans-serif;

  --tracking-display: -0.04em;     /* large heads */
  --tracking-tight: -0.01em;       /* subheads */
  --tracking-body: 0em;
  --tracking-caption: 0.005em;

  --leading-display: 1.05;
  --leading-tight: 1.2;
  --leading-body: 1.6;

  /* === Motion === */
  --duration-fast: 100ms;          /* color, opacity changes */
  --duration-normal: 200ms;        /* enter/exit, transforms */
  --duration-slow: 300ms;          /* marketing micro-interactions */

  --ease-fluid: cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0, 1);
  --ease-snappy: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1);
  --ease-out: cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);
  --ease-spring: cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1);

  /* === Elevation: rare; mostly use background contrast === */
  --shadow-pop: 0 1px 2px oklch(20% 0.04 265 / 0.06),
                0 4px 8px oklch(20% 0.04 265 / 0.04);
  --shadow-modal: 0 12px 32px oklch(20% 0.04 265 / 0.12),
                  0 4px 8px oklch(20% 0.04 265 / 0.08);
}

.dark {
  --color-bg: oklch(15% 0.02 270);
  --color-fg: oklch(95% 0.01 270);
  --color-muted: oklch(65% 0.02 270);
  --color-subtle: oklch(40% 0.02 270);
  --color-border: oklch(25% 0.01 270);
  --color-surface: oklch(18% 0.02 270);
  --color-surface-2: oklch(22% 0.02 270);
  --color-accent-soft: oklch(25% 0.06 250);
}
```

Industry packs only redefine: `--color-accent`, `--radius-button`, `--radius-card`,
`--font-display`, `--font-sans`. All other tokens stay. Read the pack file before
overriding.

---

## DEFAULT TAILWIND v4 + shadcn STACK

Recommended starting point for any web project:

- **Framework**: Next.js 15 App Router (or Vite + React 19 if no SSR needed)
- **Styling**: Tailwind v4 with `@theme` (CSS-first, no JS config)
- **Components**: shadcn/ui as primitives, customized per `references/shadcn.md`
- **Icons**: Phosphor Icons (consistent weight, broader than Lucide). Lucide acceptable
  for app chrome only.
- **Motion**: CSS animations + transitions for predetermined motion; Framer Motion
  ONLY for interruptible / gesture-driven motion.
- **Toasts**: Sonner (by Emil Kowalski).
- **Mobile sheets**: Vaul (by Emil Kowalski).
- **Command palette**: cmdk (by Paco Coursey / Rauno Freiberg).
- **Fonts**: Geist (free, OFL) as default. Override per industry pack.
- **Data viz**: Recharts for general charts, Tremor for KPI dashboards, visx for custom.

---

## ESCAPE HATCH SYNTAX

When generating code, document deviations from defaults using inline comments:

```tsx
// GRAIN OVERRIDE: industry=engineering — using 6px radius for B2B feel
<Card className="rounded-md">

// GRAIN OVERRIDE: marketing — Stripe-style gradient mesh hero
<section className="bg-gradient-to-br from-[oklch(95%_0.08_30)] via-[oklch(92%_0.1_280)] to-[oklch(94%_0.06_350)]">

// GRAIN OVERRIDE: anti-slop rule #2 — single CTA per hero (intentional break of "two CTAs")
```

Every deviation needs a reason. "It looks better" is not a reason; "industry pack
requires it" or "user explicitly asked" or "anti-slop rule conflicts with a stronger
rule" are reasons.

---

## SELF-REVIEW CHECKLIST

Before finishing a UI generation, walk this checklist out loud (or in a comment):

- [ ] **Personality**: declared category, tone, density, industry pack
- [ ] **Color**: one accent, semantic neutrals, no Tailwind default purple/indigo
- [ ] **Type**: not Inter-default; not weight 300 body; display has negative tracking
- [ ] **Radius**: systematic, not `rounded-2xl` on everything
- [ ] **Shadows**: only on elevated surfaces (modals, dropdowns), not on every card
- [ ] **Hierarchy**: weight + color drive importance, not just size
- [ ] **States**: every interactive has default / hover / focus-visible / active / disabled / loading
- [ ] **A11y**: focus rings 2px + 3:1 contrast; tap targets ≥44pt mobile / ≥24px web minimum
- [ ] **Motion**: only state-meaningful animations; reduced-motion fallback
- [ ] **SEO**: semantic HTML, one H1, meta tags, OG image (marketing only)
- [ ] **Anti-slop**: ran the 25 rules; flagged any intentional breaks with reason

If three or more items fail, regenerate the component, don't patch it.

---

## INDUSTRY PACK QUICK MATCH

| User signal | Pack |
|---|---|
| "Build a SaaS dashboard / admin panel / app screen" | `industry-saas.md` |
| "Linear / Vercel / Notion / Cal-style" | `industry-saas.md` |
| "Landing page / marketing site / homepage" | `industry-corporate.md` |
| "Apple-style / Stripe.com / agency-tier site" | `industry-corporate.md` |
| "Dashboard / monitoring / charts / tables / B2B" | `industry-engineering.md` |
| "CAD / floor plan / industrial / field tool / ruggedized" | `industry-engineering.md` |
| "iOS app / SwiftUI / iPhone UI" | `industry-mobile-ios.md` |
| "Android app / Material / Flutter" | `industry-mobile-android.md` |
| Unclear / mixed | Default to `industry-saas.md`, ask for clarification |

---

## VERSION NOTES

- **beta** (2026-05): Full rewrite. Anti-slop rules added (25). iOS 26 Liquid Glass +
  Material 3 Expressive specs integrated. Tailwind v4 `@theme` block. Industry packs
  split out. WCAG 2.2 AA enforced. Geist replaces Inter as default. Strong defaults
  with documented escape hatches.
- **v1.0** (deprecated): 12 color palettes + 8 font pairings + component specs +
  Apple HIG basics. Theme-focused. Replaced by beta.

When in doubt, the rule in `references/anti-slop-rules.md` wins. When two rules
conflict, the more specific industry pack wins. When the user explicitly overrides,
document the override and proceed.

# Industry Pack — Mobile Android (Material 3 Expressive)

For Android apps built with Jetpack Compose or XML views, and Flutter apps using
Material widgets. Anchored to **Material 3 Expressive**, announced at the
**Android Show I/O Edition** on **May 13, 2025**, with general availability in
2025–2026 across Android 16, Wear OS 6, and Material Components.

Reference points: Google's flagship apps (Gmail, Calendar, Photos, Maps,
Messages, Drive, YouTube), **Material You** showcases, **Linear Android**,
**Notion Android**, **Spotify**, **Twitter/X**, **TickTick, Todoist**, **Pocket
Casts, Plex, Tasker, Microsoft Outlook for Android**.

---

## Pack Identity

Material 3 Expressive emphasizes:

- **Spring-based motion** as the default (replacing fixed easing curves)
- **Shape morphing** — components change shape on press (pill → rounded square)
- **Larger, bolder typography** with weight variation as the primary hierarchy
  driver (Bold over Big)
- **Color expressiveness** via dynamic Material You palette generation
- **Floating Toolbars / FAB Menus** replacing bottom app bars
- **Pill-shaped buttons** as the new default
- **5 button sizes** (XS / S / M / L / XL)
- **48dp minimum tap target** (always)
- **Navigation bar now 64dp** (down from 80dp in Material 3 stock)

---

## Token Overrides

```css
:root[data-pack="android"] {
  /* M3 dynamic color — use the user's wallpaper-based primary by default */
  --color-accent: oklch(60% 0.16 280);          /* default purple, will be overridden by Material You */
  --color-accent-fg: oklch(99% 0.01 280);
  --color-accent-soft: oklch(95% 0.04 280);
  --color-accent-strong: oklch(50% 0.18 280);

  /* M3 radii */
  --radius-button: 9999px;                      /* pill */
  --radius-input: 0.25rem;                      /* 4dp */
  --radius-card: 0.75rem;                       /* 12dp */
  --radius-modal: 1.75rem;                      /* 28dp - M3 modal corner */
  --radius-bottomsheet: 1.75rem;                /* 28dp top corner only */

  /* Roboto Flex variable */
  --font-sans: "Roboto Flex", "Roboto", system-ui, sans-serif;
  --font-display: "Roboto Flex", "Roboto", system-ui, sans-serif;

  /* M3 leading */
  --leading-display: 1.12;
  --leading-headline: 1.25;
  --leading-title: 1.4;
  --leading-body: 1.45;
  --leading-label: 1.3;
}
```

For pure Material You (wallpaper-driven):
```css
:root[data-pack="android-you"] {
  --color-accent: oklch(var(--m3-primary));     /* sourced from system at runtime */
}
```

---

## The Material 3 Color System

M3 introduces **roles** instead of named colors. Each role has an `on*` companion
(for text/icon on that surface) and `*-container` variants (for backgrounds that
sit on top of the base).

### Primary palette

```
primary               — primary brand surface color (e.g., FAB background)
onPrimary             — text/icon on primary
primaryContainer      — softer container holding primary content
onPrimaryContainer    — text on primary container
```

Same pattern for `secondary`, `tertiary`, `error`, `surface`, `inverseSurface`.

### Full M3 Color Roles

```
primary, onPrimary, primaryContainer, onPrimaryContainer
secondary, onSecondary, secondaryContainer, onSecondaryContainer
tertiary, onTertiary, tertiaryContainer, onTertiaryContainer
error, onError, errorContainer, onErrorContainer
background, onBackground
surface, onSurface
surfaceVariant, onSurfaceVariant
surfaceDim, surfaceBright
surfaceContainerLowest, surfaceContainerLow, surfaceContainer,
  surfaceContainerHigh, surfaceContainerHighest
inverseSurface, inverseOnSurface, inversePrimary
outline, outlineVariant
scrim, shadow
```

13-tone palettes generate these from a single source color. With **Material You**,
that source color comes from the user's wallpaper at runtime.

### 3:1 contrast minimum for roles

All `on*` colors guarantee 3:1 contrast against their base. For body text use
`onSurface` on `surface` (always passes 4.5:1).

### In Compose

```kotlin
MaterialTheme(
  colorScheme = if (isSystemInDarkTheme()) darkColorScheme() else lightColorScheme(),
  typography = Typography(),
) {
  Surface(color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surface) {
    Text("Hello", color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurface)
  }
}
```

For dynamic Material You:
```kotlin
val colorScheme = when {
  Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.S -> {
    if (isSystemInDarkTheme()) dynamicDarkColorScheme(context)
    else dynamicLightColorScheme(context)
  }
  isSystemInDarkTheme() -> darkColorScheme()
  else -> lightColorScheme()
}
```

---

## Typography — The 15-Token Scale

M3 has 15 typography tokens (5 roles × 3 sizes). Apply via `MaterialTheme.typography`.

| Token | Size | Weight | Line height | Letter spacing |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Display Large** | 57sp | Regular 400 | 64sp | -0.25 |
| **Display Medium** | 45sp | Regular 400 | 52sp | 0 |
| **Display Small** | 36sp | Regular 400 | 44sp | 0 |
| **Headline Large** | 32sp | Regular 400 | 40sp | 0 |
| **Headline Medium** | 28sp | Regular 400 | 36sp | 0 |
| **Headline Small** | 24sp | Regular 400 | 32sp | 0 |
| **Title Large** | 22sp | Regular 400 | 28sp | 0 |
| **Title Medium** | 16sp | Medium 500 | 24sp | 0.15 |
| **Title Small** | 14sp | Medium 500 | 20sp | 0.1 |
| **Body Large** | 16sp | Regular 400 | 24sp | 0.5 |
| **Body Medium** | 14sp | Regular 400 | 20sp | 0.25 |
| **Body Small** | 12sp | Regular 400 | 16sp | 0.4 |
| **Label Large** | 14sp | Medium 500 | 20sp | 0.1 |
| **Label Medium** | 12sp | Medium 500 | 16sp | 0.5 |
| **Label Small** | 11sp | Medium 500 | 16sp | 0.5 |

In Compose:
```kotlin
Text("Title", style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleLarge)
Text("Body copy", style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyLarge)
Text("Button", style = MaterialTheme.typography.labelLarge)
```

### Roboto Flex variable

M3 Expressive (2025) ships **Roboto Flex** as the primary typeface — variable axes:
- Weight: 100–1000
- Width: 25–151%
- Optical size: 8–144
- Slant, grade, ascender height, descender depth, counter width, all variable

The "Bold over Big" principle: use weight (500 → 700) to convey hierarchy on the
same scale, instead of jumping size tokens.

### Display Flexible Variants (M3 Expressive only)

New in 2025: "Display Medium Flexible" and "Display Large Flexible" let apps use
larger, more expressive typography for product moments. Used in Google's flagship
apps for empty states, onboarding, hero moments.

---

## Buttons — 5 Sizes, 5 Styles

M3 Expressive ships **5 button sizes** and **5 button styles**.

### Sizes

| Size | Height | Use |
|---|---|---|
| **XS** | 32dp | Inline, dense lists, chips-adjacent |
| **S** | 36dp | Secondary actions in tight spaces |
| **M** | 40dp | Default |
| **L** | 48dp | Primary actions, mobile CTAs |
| **XL** | 56dp | Hero CTAs, "Continue" in onboarding |

```kotlin
Button(onClick = { }) { Text("Default M") }
Button(onClick = { }, modifier = Modifier.height(48.dp)) { Text("L") }
Button(
  onClick = { },
  modifier = Modifier.height(56.dp),
  contentPadding = PaddingValues(horizontal = 24.dp),
) { Text("XL") }
```

### Styles

| Style | Background | Use |
|---|---|---|
| **Filled** | `primary` | Primary action per screen |
| **Filled Tonal** | `secondaryContainer` | Co-equal action, softer than filled |
| **Elevated** | `surface` + shadow | Action that needs to lift off background |
| **Outlined** | transparent + outline | Secondary action |
| **Text** | transparent | Lowest-emphasis action, links |

```kotlin
Button(onClick = { }) { Text("Filled") }              // primary
FilledTonalButton(onClick = { }) { Text("Tonal") }    // secondary
ElevatedButton(onClick = { }) { Text("Elevated") }
OutlinedButton(onClick = { }) { Text("Outlined") }
TextButton(onClick = { }) { Text("Text") }
```

### Pill shape default, shape-morphs on press

M3 Expressive defaults all buttons to pill shape. On press, the shape morphs to
a slightly more rounded square via spring animation. The default is enabled when
using `ButtonDefaults.shape`.

```kotlin
Button(
  onClick = { },
  shape = ButtonDefaults.shape       // pill, morphs on press
) { Text("Action") }
```

### Icon buttons

```kotlin
IconButton(onClick = { }) {
  Icon(Icons.Default.Settings, contentDescription = "Settings")
}

// Toggleable
IconToggleButton(checked = isChecked, onCheckedChange = { isChecked = it }) {
  Icon(
    if (isChecked) Icons.Filled.Favorite else Icons.Outlined.FavoriteBorder,
    contentDescription = "Like"
  )
}
```

48dp tap target minimum. Always provide `contentDescription` for TalkBack.

---

## Navigation Bar (Bottom Nav)

Material 3 Expressive: **64dp height** (reduced from M3 standard 80dp). Active
indicator: 56dp pill behind the selected icon.

```kotlin
NavigationBar(modifier = Modifier.height(64.dp)) {
  navItems.forEach { item ->
    NavigationBarItem(
      icon = { Icon(item.icon, contentDescription = item.label) },
      label = { Text(item.label) },
      selected = currentRoute == item.route,
      onClick = { navigate(item.route) }
    )
  }
}
```

### Behaviors

- Active label not bold by default (M3 Expressive change — was bold in original M3).
- Labels always visible (selected and unselected).
- 3–5 items max. >5 items: use Navigation Drawer or Navigation Rail.

### Material You Color

Selected item indicator uses `secondaryContainer`. Icons use `onSurfaceVariant`
(unselected) → `onSecondaryContainer` (selected).

---

## Top App Bars

Four variants:

| Variant | Height | Use |
|---|---|---|
| **Small** | 64dp | Default for nested screens |
| **Center-aligned Small** | 64dp | Title centered (Material You style) |
| **Medium Flexible** | ~112dp | Important pages with extra space |
| **Large Flexible** | ~152dp | Hero pages, top-level destinations |

```kotlin
// Small top app bar
TopAppBar(
  title = { Text("Inbox") },
  navigationIcon = {
    IconButton(onClick = { /* back */ }) {
      Icon(Icons.Default.ArrowBack, contentDescription = "Back")
    }
  },
  actions = {
    IconButton(onClick = { /* search */ }) {
      Icon(Icons.Default.Search, contentDescription = "Search")
    }
  }
)

// Large top app bar that collapses on scroll
LargeTopAppBar(
  title = { Text("Inbox", style = MaterialTheme.typography.displaySmall) },
  scrollBehavior = scrollBehavior
)
```

### Scroll behaviors

- `pinnedScrollBehavior` — stays at top
- `enterAlwaysScrollBehavior` — collapses on scroll down, reappears on scroll up
- `exitUntilCollapsedScrollBehavior` — collapses to small variant, large only at top

Large Flexible is the equivalent of iOS's "large title" — big at top, collapses
to small on scroll.

---

## Bottom Sheets

Two variants:

### Standard Bottom Sheet

Inline with content (e.g., Google Maps location details). Always visible at
collapsed state, expands on drag.

```kotlin
BottomSheetScaffold(
  sheetContent = { LocationDetails() },
  sheetPeekHeight = 128.dp,
) { padding ->
  MapView(padding)
}
```

### Modal Bottom Sheet

Overlay with scrim. Used for actions, filters, share sheets.

```kotlin
val sheetState = rememberModalBottomSheetState()
```

## Motion — Springs Replace Easing

M3 Expressive replaces fixed-duration easing with **spring physics tokens** as the
default for important transitions.

### Spring tokens

```kotlin
// In Compose, the default for state animations

  dampingRatio = Spring.DampingRatioNoBouncy,
  stiffness = Spring.StiffnessMedium
)

// Categories

Spring.DampingRatioMediumBouncy
Spring.DampingRatioLowBouncy
Spring.DampingRatioNoBouncy

Spring.StiffnessHigh
Spring.StiffnessMedium
Spring.StiffnessMediumLow
Spring.StiffnessLow
Spring.StiffnessVeryLow
```

### Easing curves (still available for non-spring)

```kotlin

MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedCubicBezier            // important transitions
MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedDecelerateCubicBezier  // incoming elements
MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedAccelerateCubicBezier  // outgoing
```

### Duration tokens

```
short1 = 50ms
short2 = 100ms
short3 = 150ms
short4 = 200ms
medium1 = 250ms
medium2 = 300ms
medium3 = 350ms
medium4 = 400ms
long1 = 450ms
long2 = 500ms
long3 = 550ms
long4 = 600ms
extraLong1 = 700ms
extraLong2 = 800ms
extraLong3 = 900ms
extraLong4 = 1000ms
```

Default for UI feedback: `short3` (150ms) to `medium1` (250ms).

- **Spring**: drag, gesture release, shape morphing, important state changes.
- **Easing**: enter/exit, predictable transitions, simple property changes.

```
medium = 12dp
large = 16dp
extraLarge = 28dp
```

Android 12+ supports user-wallpaper-derived themes. Opt in:

```kotlin
val colorScheme = when {
  Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.S -> {
    val context = LocalContext.current
    if (darkTheme) dynamicDarkColorScheme(context)
    else dynamicLightColorScheme(context)
  }
  darkTheme -> darkColorScheme()
  else -> lightColorScheme()
}
```

For apps where brand identity is critical, **don't** use dynamic color — provide a
fixed `ColorScheme`. For consumer apps where personalization is welcome (Calendar,
Notes, Messages), opt in.

**1.** **48dp minimum tap targets.** Material guideline, hard floor.

**2.** **Use Material Components**, don't reinvent buttons, sliders, switches.

**3.** **Roboto Flex** as the default typeface; weight contrast > size contrast.

**4.** **Pill-shaped buttons** as default (M3 Expressive).

**5.** **Bottom navigation 64dp**, max 5 items, labels always visible.

**6.** **Large flexible top app bars** for top-level destinations; small for drill-down.

**7.** **Modal bottom sheets** for actions/filters, not centered dialogs.

**8.** **Spring physics** for state-meaningful motion, not fixed easing.

**9.** **Shape morphing on button press** (M3 Expressive default).

**10.** **Dynamic color** for consumer apps; fixed scheme for brand-critical apps.

**11.** **FAB Menu** for multi-action primary; FAB for single primary.

**12.** **Floating Toolbars** for contextual action sets (deprecated Bottom App Bar).

**13.** **Material 3 list item heights** strict: 48 / 56 / 64 / 72 / 88dp.

**14.** **TalkBack labels** on every Icon-only button (`contentDescription`).

**15.** **Test with TalkBack on**, large font size (200%), and dark theme.

```dart
        ),
```

## Apple vs Material — The Contradictions Table

Cross-platform apps must respect platform conventions. Here's where the systems
diverge:

| Concern | iOS | Material 3 |
|---|---|---|
| Primary action position | Trailing (right) in nav | Bottom right (FAB) or right in app bar |
| Modal style | Bottom sheet with detents | Modal bottom sheet OR dialog |
| Back navigation | Top-left chevron + label | Top-left arrow icon |
| Top nav title | Large title that collapses | Small or Large Flexible app bar |
| Tap target | 44pt | 48dp |
| Font | SF Pro variable | Roboto Flex variable |
| Hierarchy driver | Size + weight (Dynamic Type) | Weight > size (Bold over Big) |
| Button shape default | Capsule (`.buttonBorderShape(.capsule)`) | Pill |
| Motion default | Smooth ease | Spring physics |
| Tab bar height | ~49pt (now glass, minimize on scroll) | 64dp (down from 80dp) |
| Empty space treatment | Generous | Slightly tighter |
| Color generation | Custom or system blue | Material You from wallpaper |

For cross-platform: provide a platform-aware shim layer. Don't ship Material UI to
iOS or Cupertino UI to Android.

---

## Hard Bans for Android Pack

- ❌ iOS-style centered dialogs on Android (use bottom sheets).
- ❌ Tap targets below 48dp.
- ❌ Hardcoded colors that ignore Material You / dynamic theming.
- ❌ Bottom app bars (deprecated in M3 Expressive; use Docked/Floating Toolbar).
- ❌ Old M3 navigation bar heights (80dp) — use 64dp.
- ❌ Bold selected labels in nav bar (M3 Expressive changed this default).
- ❌ Fixed-duration easing for state-meaningful transitions (use springs).
- ❌ Pre-Roboto-Flex fonts (Roboto, Noto Sans) when Roboto Flex is available.
- ❌ Ignoring Dynamic Type / font scale settings.
- ❌ Snackbars stacking (one at a time, latest wins).
- ❌ FABs that don't expand to FAB Menu when multiple actions exist.
- ❌ Custom toggles / sliders when Material variants suffice.

For Android apps built with Jetpack Compose or XML views, and Flutter apps using
Material widgets. Anchored to **Material 3 Expressive**, announced at the
**Android Show I/O Edition** on **May 13, 2025**, with general availability in
2025–2026 across Android 16, Wear OS 6, and Material Components.

**Notion Android**, **Spotify**, **Twitter/X**, **TickTick, Todoist**, **Pocket

## Pack Identity

Material 3 Expressive emphasizes:

- **Spring-based motion** as the default (replacing fixed easing curves)
- **Shape morphing** — components change shape on press (pill → rounded square)
- **Larger, bolder typography** with weight variation as the primary hierarchy

M3 introduces **roles** instead of named colors. Each role has an `on*` companion
(for text/icon on that surface) and `*-container` variants (for backgrounds that
sit on top of the base).

### Primary palette

```
primary               — primary brand surface color (e.g., FAB background)
onPrimary             — text/icon on primary
primaryContainer      — softer container holding primary content
onPrimaryContainer    — text on primary container
```

Same pattern for `secondary`, `tertiary`, `error`, `surface`, `inverseSurface`.

### Full M3 Color Roles

```
primary, onPrimary, primaryContainer, onPrimaryContainer
secondary, onSecondary, secondaryContainer, onSecondaryContainer
tertiary, onTertiary, tertiaryContainer, onTertiaryContainer
error, onError, errorContainer, onErrorContainer
background, onBackground
surface, onSurface
surfaceVariant, onSurfaceVariant
surfaceDim, surfaceBright
surfaceContainerLowest, surfaceContainerLow, surfaceContainer,
  surfaceContainerHigh, surfaceContainerHighest
inverseSurface, inverseOnSurface, inversePrimary
outline, outlineVariant
scrim, shadow
```

13-tone palettes generate these from a single source color. With **Material You**,
that source color comes from the user's wallpaper at runtime.

All `on*` colors guarantee 3:1 contrast against their base. For body text use
`onSurface` on `surface` (always passes 4.5:1).

```kotlin

) {

}
```

```kotlin

Spring.DampingRatioNoBouncy

Spring.StiffnessHigh
Spring.StiffnessMedium
Spring.StiffnessMediumLow
Spring.StiffnessLow
Spring.StiffnessVeryLow
```

### Easing curves (still available for non-spring)

```kotlin
MotionTokens.EasingStandardCubicBezier              // cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)
MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedCubicBezier            // important transitions
MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedDecelerateCubicBezier  // incoming elements
MotionTokens.EasingEmphasizedAccelerateCubicBezier  // outgoing
```

### Duration tokens

```
short1 = 50ms
short2 = 100ms
short3 = 150ms
short4 = 200ms
medium1 = 250ms
medium2 = 300ms
medium3 = 350ms
medium4 = 400ms
long1 = 450ms
long2 = 500ms
long3 = 550ms
long4 = 600ms
extraLong1 = 700ms
extraLong2 = 800ms
extraLong3 = 900ms
extraLong4 = 1000ms
```

Default for UI feedback: `short3` (150ms) to `medium1` (250ms).

### When to use spring vs easing

- **Spring**: drag, gesture release, shape morphing, important state changes.
- **Easing**: enter/exit, predictable transitions, simple property changes.

---

## Shape System

M3 has a shape system with five named tokens:

```
extraSmall = 4dp
small = 8dp
medium = 12dp
large = 16dp
extraLarge = 28dp
full = 9999dp (pill)
```

Applied per-component default:
- Buttons → full (pill)
- Cards → medium (12dp)
- Modals / sheets → extraLarge (28dp)
- Inputs → extraSmall (4dp)
- Snackbars → extraSmall

In Compose:
```kotlin
Card(shape = MaterialTheme.shapes.medium) { ... }
```

---

## Snackbars (the Toast equivalent)

```kotlin
val snackbarHostState = remember { SnackbarHostState() }
val scope = rememberCoroutineScope()

Scaffold(
  snackbarHost = { SnackbarHost(snackbarHostState) }
) { padding ->
  Button(onClick = {
    scope.launch {
      snackbarHostState.showSnackbar(
        message = "Project saved",
        actionLabel = "Undo",
        duration = SnackbarDuration.Short
      )
    }
  }) { Text("Save") }
}
```

- Position: bottom of screen.
- Duration: Short (~4s) / Long (~7s) / Indefinite.
- One snackbar at a time.
- Includes action when reversible.

---

## Material You Dynamic Color

Android 12+ supports user-wallpaper-derived themes. Opt in:

```kotlin
val colorScheme = when {
  Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.S -> {
    val context = LocalContext.current
    if (darkTheme) dynamicDarkColorScheme(context)
    else dynamicLightColorScheme(context)
  }
  darkTheme -> darkColorScheme()
  else -> lightColorScheme()
}
```

For apps where brand identity is critical, **don't** use dynamic color — provide a
fixed `ColorScheme`. For consumer apps where personalization is welcome (Calendar,
Notes, Messages), opt in.

---

## The 15 Android Mobile Rules

**1.** **48dp minimum tap targets.** Material guideline, hard floor.

**2.** **Use Material Components**, don't reinvent buttons, sliders, switches.

**3.** **Roboto Flex** as the default typeface; weight contrast > size contrast.

**4.** **Pill-shaped buttons** as default (M3 Expressive).

**5.** **Bottom navigation 64dp**, max 5 items, labels always visible.

**6.** **Large flexible top app bars** for top-level destinations; small for drill-down.

**7.** **Modal bottom sheets** for actions/filters, not centered dialogs.

**8.** **Spring physics** for state-meaningful motion, not fixed easing.

**9.** **Shape morphing on button press** (M3 Expressive default).

**10.** **Dynamic color** for consumer apps; fixed scheme for brand-critical apps.

**11.** **FAB Menu** for multi-action primary; FAB for single primary.

**12.** **Floating Toolbars** for contextual action sets (deprecated Bottom App Bar).

**13.** **Material 3 list item heights** strict: 48 / 56 / 64 / 72 / 88dp.

**14.** **TalkBack labels** on every Icon-only button (`contentDescription`).

**15.** **Test with TalkBack on**, large font size (200%), and dark theme.

---

## Flutter Material (cross-platform Android target)

```dart
MaterialApp(
  theme: ThemeData(
    useMaterial3: true,
    colorSchemeSeed: Color(0xFF5E6AD2),
    typography: Typography.material2021(),
  ),
  home: Scaffold(
    appBar: AppBar(title: Text('Home')),
    body: ListView(
      children: [
        ListTile(
          title: Text('Item'),
          trailing: Icon(Icons.chevron_right),
        ),
      ],
    ),
    floatingActionButton: FloatingActionButton(
      onPressed: () { },
      child: Icon(Icons.add),
    ),
    bottomNavigationBar: NavigationBar(
      destinations: [
        NavigationDestination(icon: Icon(Icons.home), label: 'Home'),
        NavigationDestination(icon: Icon(Icons.search), label: 'Search'),
      ],
      selectedIndex: 0,
      onDestinationSelected: (i) { },
    ),
  ),
)
```

Flutter's M3 support as of 2026 includes most M3 Expressive components, with FAB
Menu and Floating Toolbar landing in 2025–2026 updates.

---

## Apple vs Material — The Contradictions Table

Cross-platform apps must respect platform conventions. Here's where the systems
diverge:

| Concern | iOS | Material 3 |
|---|---|---|
| Primary action position | Trailing (right) in nav | Bottom right (FAB) or right in app bar |
| Modal style | Bottom sheet with detents | Modal bottom sheet OR dialog |
| Back navigation | Top-left chevron + label | Top-left arrow icon |
| Top nav title | Large title that collapses | Small or Large Flexible app bar |
| Tap target | 44pt | 48dp |
| Font | SF Pro variable | Roboto Flex variable |
| Hierarchy driver | Size + weight (Dynamic Type) | Weight > size (Bold over Big) |
| Button shape default | Capsule (`.buttonBorderShape(.capsule)`) | Pill |
| Motion default | Smooth ease | Spring physics |
| Tab bar height | ~49pt (now glass, minimize on scroll) | 64dp (down from 80dp) |
| Empty space treatment | Generous | Slightly tighter |
| Color generation | Custom or system blue | Material You from wallpaper |

For cross-platform: provide a platform-aware shim layer. Don't ship Material UI to
iOS or Cupertino UI to Android.

---

## Hard Bans for Android Pack

- ❌ iOS-style centered dialogs on Android (use bottom sheets).
- ❌ Tap targets below 48dp.
- ❌ Hardcoded colors that ignore Material You / dynamic theming.
- ❌ Bottom app bars (deprecated in M3 Expressive; use Docked/Floating Toolbar).
- ❌ Old M3 navigation bar heights (80dp) — use 64dp.
- ❌ Bold selected labels in nav bar (M3 Expressive changed this default).
- ❌ Fixed-duration easing for state-meaningful transitions (use springs).
- ❌ Pre-Roboto-Flex fonts (Roboto, Noto Sans) when Roboto Flex is available.
- ❌ Ignoring Dynamic Type / font scale settings.
- ❌ Snackbars stacking (one at a time, latest wins).
- ❌ FABs that don't expand to FAB Menu when multiple actions exist.
- ❌ Custom toggles / sliders when Material variants suffice.
